events.title: Palisade 0.49: Workshop maps, LAN beta and ally support
events.summary: Steam Workshop Publish maps from the editor to the Steam Workshop, subscribe to maps other players made, and play them in Skirmish. A Workshop map shows the creator name Steam reports for it. Map editor Painting, camera controls, undo and saving are faster, and the tools fit smaller windows. New Map shows a thumbnail of the template with its start sites marked. Play in the editor starts the battle directly, without a second briefing. A map's author field is now Credit, and library cards label it

events.title: Palisade 0.40.2
events.summary: Short Naval Landings cost less, based on the sea route. Previews show the quoted cost. Tiny coastal islands have been removed or joined to nearby land; larger rivers and straits remain separate. Attack previews show committed troops. Help explains the 25% share of remaining reserve and independent fronts. Neutral expansion depends on committed troops, reducing the advantage of repeated clicks or splitting forces. Palisades can enclose buildings, and AI realms make better use of defensive walls.

events.title: Palisade 0.28.7
events.summary: The demo difficulty menu shows Standard, Hardened, and Relentless without clipping at Large interface scale. Impossible stays locked as a full-game preview; completing the demo does not unlock it. W pans the camera up again. Battlefield actions use Q/4 for Naval Landing, E/5 for Cavalry Charge, and R/6 for Palisades. Typing in a text field no longer triggers game shortcuts. Each theatre has its own map identity, historical framing, authored starting positions, objectives, pressure events, and campaign rewards. events.title: Palisade 0.3.0 — Supply Lines & Command
events.summary: Highlights Supply and isolation — Naval Landings now build visible yards and supply routes. Cut-off territory attacks at half strength and is twice as easy to capture until reconnected; threatened routes can be recovered before they collapse. Capitals matter more — Three upgrade tiers bring stronger defence, wider protection, and 6/8/10-second occupations.
